messages.author: f97d21be02e5ed9b
messages.subject: Truncated Normal Producing Strange Results
parts:
Hello,

I'm trying to run a model that includes a directed random walk component with a truncated normal, but the MCMC runs into issues after a few iterations and produces +/- INF for the posterior estimates. This model works in JAGS but not in NIMBLE. 

In my model, s refers to a location, with the 1st column = x coordinate, 2nd column = y coordinate. East, north, xmin, xmax, ymin and ymax are all known values. I think the problem happens right here:
s[i,1,t] ~ T(dnorm((s[i,1,t-1]+omega*east[pix[i,t-1]]), 1/(k^2)), xmin, xmax) 
s[i,2,t] ~  T(dnorm((s[i,2,t-1]+omega*north[pix[i,t-1]]),1/(k^2)), ymin, ymax)

What I think is happening is that sometimes the sampler chooses a combination of values for omega/k that creates a normal distribution where all of the probability is outside of the min/max truncation, so the MCMC can't calculate a new location. Is there some way to avoid this issue or a better way to specify this type of model? 

My real model has many more moving parts, but I've attached a simplified example below that still produces the same error. 

Any advice would be greatly appreciated. 

Best,

Heather

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: Truncated Normal Producing Strange Results
parts:
hi Heather,

JAGS tends to use slice samplers by default whereas NIMBLE uses Metropolis samplers, and slice samplers may work better in such cases where certain parameter values may produce numerical issues. So without having looked in any detail at your model, my suggestion would be to assign slice samplers for various potentially problematic parameters such as omega and k.

-chris

And, by the same token, nimble's default samplers can be more sensitive to choice of valid, reasonable, and complete inits, so discrepancies like you're seeing are sometimes resolved by attention to the inits.
HTH!
Perry

messages.author: f97d21be02e5ed9b
messages.subject: Re: Truncated Normal Producing Strange Results
parts:
Just in case anyone else comes across this problem, the solution was all about sampler choice. I simply had to tell NIMBLE to jointly sample s[,1:2] (the x and y coordinates of each point) and the error went away. Seems a little foolish now in retrospect. 

My solution:
adaptInterval = 200
SamplerScale <- 0.05
mcmcbirds$removeSampler(paste0("s[",1:nind,", 1:2, 1:",nocc,"]"))
for(i in 1:nind){
  for(tt in 1:occ){
    mcmcbirds$addSampler(target = paste0("s[",i,", 1:2, ",tt,"]"),
                         type = 'RW_block', silent=TRUE,
                         control = list(adaptInterval = adaptInterval, propCov=diag(2), scale=SamplerScale, adaptScaleOnly=TRUE))
  }
